Answer: E
Reason: The chest radiograph demonstrates unilateral hyperlucency and hyperinflation of the right lung with a small, attenuated right hilum, which are hallmark features of Swyer–James–MacLeod syndrome (post-infectious bronchiolitis obliterans). This condition typically presents with a history of recurrent lung infections in childhood and can be associated with airway abnormalities like laryngomalacia.
